content: 1. If a drug that is known to prolong the QT interval must be used, it is recommended to perform more frequent ECG monitoring. Both vemurafenib and azithromycin increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Concomitant use of vemurafenib with drugs that prolong the QT interval is not recommended. 2. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of venetoclax by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If a P-gp inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor closely for signs of venetoclax toxicities. 3. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when vilanterol is coadministered with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 4. Azithromycin increases the levels of afatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Reduce the afatinib daily dose by 10 mg if not tolerated when coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. 5. Both azithromycin and alfuzosin increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of azithromycin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 7. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of amiodarone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Both amitriptyline and azithromycin increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Both amoxapine and azithromycin increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of apomorphine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of arformoterol by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Both azithromycin and artemether/lumefantrine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of asenapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Both asenapine transdermal and azithromycin increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of atorvastatin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. If this combination is used, closely monitor for evidence of atorvastatin toxicity (e.g., muscle aches or pains, renal dysfunction). 16. Azithromycin decreases the level or effect of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Azithromycin decreases the level or effect of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 18. Both azithromycin and bedaquiline increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. ECG should be monitored closely. 19. Azithromycin increases the levels of berotralstat by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Azithromycin increases the levels of betrixaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Decrease the betrixaban dose to 80 mg PO once, then 40 mg PO daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. 21. Azithromycin decreases the level or effect of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of azithromycin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 23. Azithromycin decreases the effects of cefdinir by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 24. Azithromycin decreases the effects of cefditoren by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 25. Azithromycin decreases the effects of cefoxitin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 26. Azithromycin decreases the effects of cefpodoxime by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 27. Azithromycin decreases the effects of cefuroxime by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 28. Azithromycin increases the levels of ceritinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of cetirizine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of chloroquine by prolonging the QTc interval. Chloroquine also increases the toxicity of azithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Both chlorpromazine and azithromycin increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of ciprofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Both azithromycin and citalopram increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended, along with drugs that may prolong the QT interval. 34. Both azithromycin and clarithromycin increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of clofazimine by prolonging the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 36. Both clomipramine and azithromycin increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Azithromycin decreases the level or effect of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 38. Both crizotinib and azithromycin increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of crizotinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of cyclosporine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of dabigatran by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. For atrial fibrillation, avoid coadministering dabigatran with P-gp inhibitors if CrCl <30 mL/min. For DVT/PE treatment, avoid coadministering dabigatran with P-gp inhibitors if CrCl <50 mL/min. 41. Both desipramine and azithromycin increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of deutetrabenazine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. Certain circumstances may increase the risk of torsades de pointes and/or sudden death in association with drugs that prolong the QTc interval (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia, coadministration with other drugs that prolong the QTc interval, presence of congenital QT prolongation). 43. Both dichlorphenamide and azithromycin decrease serum potassium. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Azithromycin decreases the level or effect of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. An alternate or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. 45. Both azithromycin and disopyramide increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 46. Both azithromycin and dofetilide increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Both doxepin and azithromycin increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Both azithromycin and droperidol increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of duvelisib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of edoxaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, decrease the dose to 30 mg PO once daily. For NVAF, no dose reduction is recommended. ...
